financial_summary: FLEX LNG Ltd. is a small-cap energy business with a $1.4B market cap on $348M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -0% over the past three years — essentially flat, and a business treading water is rarely a path to compounding.
Returns on capital run at 9% against a 8% cost of capital, which means the business barely earns its keep economically.

The business throws off $141M in free cash flow — roughly 40 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.88× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is heavy at 5.6× net debt/EBITDA, and leverage like that is what turns a bad year into a permanent loss, and thin 1.9× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Management returns a meaningful 11.8% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 43% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 4.6× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
